# Binomial distribution {#sec-binomial}

{{< include ../preamble.qmd >}}

## Concepts and intuitions {.unnumbered}

## Formal {.unnumbered}
$$
P(X = k) = \binom{n}{k} p^k (1-p)^{n-k}
$${#eq-binomial}

$$
\binom{n}{k} = \frac{n!}{k!(n-k)!}
$${#eq-bincoeff}

## Examples {.unnumbered}

```{r}
#| code-fold: false
#| fig-cap: "Binomial Distribution - Probability Mass Function with different parameters"
#| label: fig-binomial-dist

# Set up the plot
plot(NULL, xlim = c(-1, 21), ylim = c(0, 0.35),
     xlab = "x", ylab = "P(X = x)",
     main = "Binomial Distribution - Probability Mass Function")

# Define colors and parameters
colors <- c("blue", "red", "green")
params <- list(
  list(n = 10, p = 0.2, label = "n=10, p=0.2"),
  list(n = 10, p = 0.5, label = "n=10, p=0.5"),
  list(n = 20, p = 0.2, label = "n=20, p=0.2")
)

# Plot each distribution
for (i in seq_along(params)) {
  n <- params[[i]]$n
  p <- params[[i]]$p
  label <- params[[i]]$label
  color <- colors[i]

  # Calculate PMF for each value of x
  x <- 0:n
  pmf <- dbinom(x, n, p)

  # Connect points with thin lines and add points
  lines(x, pmf, col = color, lwd = 1, lty = 1)
  points(x, pmf, pch = 21, bg = color, col = color, cex = 1.2)
}

# Add legend
legend("topright",
       legend = c("n=10, p=0.2", "n=10, p=0.5", "n=20, p=0.2"),
       col = colors,
       lwd = 2,
       pch = 21,
       pt.bg = colors,
       cex = 0.9)

# Add grid for better readability
grid()
```
